prerequisites: Knowledge of fundamental aspects concerning chemical bonds, state of matter, the most common engineering metallic materials, heat treatments, technical drawings, and stress and strain states is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of foundry technology as a method to vary the shape of semi-finished products and the consequent choice of different casting techniques.
Ability to recognize and avoid the most common defects of castings.
Knowledge of the mechanism of plastic deformation of metallic materials and the most common processing techniques.

The course enables students to acquire advanced knowledge of the processes required to transform raw material into finished products with market value, through processes carried out on machines or systems.

This knowledge, by integrating notions acquired in the courses of material science, machine design, and mechanical drawing, will form the insights that will enrich knowledge and operational capabilities in the field of manufacturing processes in mechanics, so that the student acquires a clear awareness of the wider multidisciplinary context of engineering.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION. Definition, the product life cycle, the main manufacturing processes, the relationship between processes and materials, the technological system, and the accuracy of transformations.

METAL CASTING. Fundamentals of casting and classification, mold, pattern, core, undercut, pouring of the molten metal, cooling effects, and castability. Expendable mold casting processes: sand casting and mold making, other expendable mold casting processes. Permanent mold casting processes: the basic permanent-mold process, low-pressure casting, die casting (cold-chamber and hot-chamber die casting).

METAL FORMING. Fundamentals of plasticity, constitutive models, tension test, axisymmetric and plane strain compression tests, friction, workability, classification of metalworking processes. Forging: definitions, forgeability, forging machines, factors affecting the die filling, flashing, open die forging, close die forging and other related processes, flash formation, pre-forming, forging forces. Sheet forming: anisotropy and formability of sheet metals. Shearing, blanking, and punching. Sheet bending: V bending, elastic spring back, bending force, and other bending processes. Deep drawing of axisymmetric parts: engineering analysis, choice of process parameters, calculation of the blank diameter. Deep drawing of non-axisymmetric parts and sheet stamping.

MATERIAL REMOVAL PROCESSES. Definitions, cutting and feed motions, cutting parameters, theory of chip formation in metal machining, actual chip formation, types of chip, build-up edge, cutting forces, specific energy, thermal aspects in cutting, three-dimensional cutting, machinability, tool wear, and tool life, cutting tool technology.
Welding: general aspects of welding. Welding techniques: Arc welding, TIG, MIG, MAG, diffusion bonding, chemical, laser welding, braising, and solid-state welding FSW.

assessment_methods.method: Written test (3 open-answer questions and/or exercises)

assessment_rules: The written test consists of 10 multi-choice questions and 4 open-answer questions and/or exercises. Multi-choice questions weigh 10/30, while the three open-ended questions have a weight of 5 points each. A minimum of eighteen points is required to pass. The maximum grade, thirty points cum laude, is awarded for complete mastery of the subject, autonomous exposition, and appropriate technical language. Mid-term exams and in-itinerary tests are also part of the assessment.
